hotel.name: Vatican City, Borgo district Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Use the time on the plane to rest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Rome airport at 13:00. Take the Leonardo Express train or a budget bus (€6–8) to the city center. Check into your Boutique Stay in Vatican City, Borgo district. After settling in, take a relaxing orientation walk through the Borgo neighborhood — stroll along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for a first glimpse of the iconic basilica and piazza. Enjoy the atmosphere without paying any entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming streets of Borgo and Prati neighborhood on foot. Visit Castel Sant'Angelo from the outside (free exterior view) and walk along the Tiber riverbank at sunset for beautiful golden-hour views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto (€2–3) at a local bar near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and affordable lunch near the hotel — try a local pizza al taglio (pizza by the slice) shop in Prati for around €4–6.
meals.dinner: Dine at a casual trattoria in the Prati neighborhood. Look for a fixed-price 'menu turistico' (€12–15) offering pasta, a main, and water/bread. Try cacio e pepe or carbonara, classic Roman pasta dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Focus on settling in, orienting yourself, and recovering from travel. Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport pass (€7–12) at the airport or metro station for cost-effective travel in the coming days.

day_by_day.morning: Start early at the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel. Book tickets online in advance (€17–20) to skip the line. Spend 2–3 hours marveling at the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Entry to St. Peter's Basilica is FREE — don't miss it after your museum visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Climb to the top of St. Peter's Dome (€6 on foot, €8 by elevator) for panoramic views over Rome — one of the best budget views in the city. Afterward, walk across the Tiber to the lively Campo de' Fiori market square (market runs until ~2 PM). Explore the square and surrounding streets.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the nearby Piazza Navona — one of Rome's most beautiful baroque squares, free to visit. Watch street artists, admire Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, and soak in the evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Bar/café near the hotel — espresso and cornetto for €2–3. A Roman classic morning ritual.
meals.lunch: Grab street food at Campo de' Fiori market or a nearby sandwich shop (panino) for €4–6. Try a suppli (fried rice ball) — a Roman street food staple.
meals.dinner: Budget trattoria near Piazza Navona or Trastevere. Try pasta all'amatriciana or gricia for €8–12. Avoid restaurants directly on the piazza as they charge tourist premiums.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums are closed on Sundays (except last Sunday of the month when entry is free but extremely crowded). Book tickets online at least a few days in advance. Dress code required for the Basilica — cover shoulders and knees.

day_by_day.morning: Head to the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill — a combined ticket costs around €16–18 and covers all three sites. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and heat. Spend 2–3 hours exploring ancient Rome's most iconic landmark and the sprawling ruins of the Forum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to the Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) for free — enjoy the stunning view overlooking the Roman Forum. Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15), the world's oldest public museums, housing masterpieces including the original Marcus Aurelius equestrian statue and Caravaggio paintings. Alternatively, skip the museum and enjoy the free hilltop views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Trastevere neighborhood (30-minute walk or short bus ride) — one of Rome's most charming and authentic districts. Wander the cobblestone streets, peek into the beautiful Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (free entry), and enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Local bar near the hotel — espresso, cornetto, and fresh-squeezed orange juice for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic or grab food from a nearby alimentari (deli) before heading to the Colosseum. Eat near the Circus Maximus or in a shaded spot by the Forum. Budget €5–7.
meals.dinner: Eat dinner in Trastevere — try Da Enzo al 29 or a similar traditional Roman trattoria. Pasta dishes from €8–12. Share a carafe of house wine (€4–6) to keep costs down.

day_by_day.notes: The Colosseum area gets extremely hot in summer — bring water, sunscreen, and a hat. Pre-book Colosseum tickets online to avoid long queues. The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill are included in the same ticket and are worth at least 1–2 hours of exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Borghese Gallery (€15, reservation mandatory) — one of Rome's finest art collections featuring Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in a stunning villa setting. Reservations are required and slots fill up weeks in advance. Afterward, take a free stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's answer to Central Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down the Spanish Steps (free) and explore the upscale Tridente neighborhood. Window-shop along Via Condotti and toss a coin into the iconic Trevi Fountain (free). Visit the Pantheon — entry is now €5 but it remains one of the world's best-preserved ancient buildings. Marvel at the 2,000-year-old unreinforced concrete dome.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — one of Rome's oldest and most atmospheric quarters. Walk along the ancient ruins of the Portico d'Ottavia (free, outdoor). The area is quiet and authentic in the evenings.

meals.breakfast: Try a local pasticceria for a slightly more indulgent breakfast — a sfogliatella or maritozzo (cream-filled bun, a Roman specialty) with coffee for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Grab lunch near the Pantheon — avoid the tourist traps directly around it. Walk one or two streets away for affordable pizza al taglio or a simple pasta at a local bar (€6–9).
meals.dinner: Dine in the Jewish Ghetto — try carciofi alla giudia (Jewish-style fried artichokes, a Roman specialty) and pasta at a local restaurant. Budget €12–16 for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked well in advance — check their official website. The gallery limits visitors to 2-hour time slots. Villa Borghese gardens are perfect for a midday picnic if you want to save on lunch costs.

day_by_day.morning: Take a free morning to explore the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's historic working-class district and the heart of Roman food culture. Visit the Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio) — an authentic local market (not touristy) with incredible food stalls. Sample local cheeses, cured meats, supplì, and fresh produce. Budget €5–10 for tastings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) — a hauntingly beautiful and peaceful garden cemetery where poets Keats and Shelley are buried. Entry is by donation (€3 suggested). Nearby, see the Pyramid of Cestius — a real ancient Roman pyramid embedded in the city walls, free to view from outside. Then head to Aventine Hill to visit the Knights of Malta Keyhole (free) — peer through the keyhole for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome, one of Rome's best-kept secrets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Trastevere or Pigneto neighborhood for a laid-back Friday evening. Join locals for an aperitivo — many bars offer a free buffet of snacks with a drink purchase (€5–8 for a Spritz or glass of wine with snacks).

meals.breakfast: Eat at the Testaccio Market — grab a fresh cornetto and coffee from a market vendor for €2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat lunch at the Testaccio Market — try the famous supplì, a trapizzino (Roman street food sandwich), or a panino with porchetta. Full satisfying lunch for €6–9.
meals.dinner: Aperitivo buffet for a light dinner (€5–8), or find a budget pizzeria in Trastevere for a full Neapolitan-style pizza (€7–10). Rome has excellent pizza by the slice and full-pie options.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio Market is open Monday–Saturday until about 2:00 PM — perfect for a morning visit. This is one of the most authentic food experiences in Rome and a highlight for food lovers. The Aventine Keyhole often has a short queue — visit early afternoon to avoid waiting.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning trip to the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Moderna e Contemporanea (GNAM) in Villa Borghese — a lesser-visited but excellent modern art museum (€10 entry). Features works by Modigliani, Klimt, Cézanne, and major Italian artists. Enjoy the peaceful gardens surrounding it afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Pigneto or Ostiense neighborhoods — Rome's hipster and street art districts. Walk along Via del Porto Fluviale to see incredible large-scale street murals (free, outdoor art). Visit the MACRO (Museum of Contemporary Art of Rome) if interested (€5–10). These neighborhoods offer an authentic, non-touristy side of modern Rome.
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward the historic center for a final grand evening stroll. Walk from Piazza del Popolo down the Via del Corso, then to Piazza di Spagna, and end at the illuminated Trevi Fountain at night — magical and less crowded than daytime. Gelato from a quality gelateria nearby for €2–3.

meals.breakfast: Local café near the hotel for the usual espresso and cornetto (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Ostiense or Pigneto area — try a local pizzeria or trattoria frequented by Romans, not tourists. Budget €8–12 for pasta and a drink.
meals.dinner: Splurge slightly on your second-to-last night — find a mid-range trattoria in the historic center or near Campo de' Fiori. Try saltimbocca alla romana or abbacchio (Roman lamb) for €14–18 for a full meal with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings in Rome's historic center are lively and festive — perfect for a final evening stroll. The Trevi Fountain is particularly beautiful when illuminated at night. Always choose gelaterias that display natural-looking colors (not fluorescent) and keep gelato in covered metal containers — signs of quality.

day_by_day.morning: Visit one of Rome's stunning baroque churches — all free to enter. Start with San Luigi dei Francesi (home to three Caravaggio masterpieces — free), then walk to Sant'Ignazio di Loyola (stunning trompe-l'oeil ceiling fresco — free), and finish at Santa Maria Sopra Minerva (Rome's only Gothic church, with a Michelangelo sculpture — free). A full morning of world-class art at zero cost.
day_by_day.afternoon: If it's the last Sunday of the month, Vatican Museums offer free entry (expect very long queues — arrive 1–2 hours before opening). Otherwise, spend the afternoon doing last-minute souvenir shopping at Campo de' Fiori or Porta Portese flea market (open Sunday mornings until 2 PM — great for vintage finds and budget souvenirs). Take a final walk along the Tiber and through your beloved Borgo neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in the Prati neighborhood near your hotel — a relaxed final meal before departure. Toast to a wonderful Roman holiday with a glass of local Frascati white wine or a Peroni beer.

meals.breakfast: Final Roman breakfast at your favorite local bar — espresso doppio and a fresh cornetto. Savor the ritual one last time (€2–3).
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Campo de' Fiori or Porta Portese — grab street food, a panino, or pizza al taglio for €5–7. Keep it casual and affordable.
meals.dinner: Final dinner in Prati — choose a trattoria you noticed during your stay. Order a classic Roman pasta (carbonara, cacio e pepe, or amatriciana) and a dolce (dessert) like tiramisu or panna cotta to end the trip on a sweet note. Budget €12–16.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is early the next morning, pack your bags the night before. Keep transport options to the airport in mind — the Leonardo Express runs from Roma Termini and is reliable. Budget approximately €14 for the express train. Overall budget tip: Rome's greatest treasures — its piazzas, fountains, churches, and street life — are largely free. Prioritize spending on 2–3 key paid attractions and save on food by eating like a local.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so morning is in transit. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini, then connect to your hotel in the Vatican/Borgo district. Allow ~90 minutes for arrival, baggage, and transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Neighborhood Orientation Walk: After checking in, take a leisurely stroll through the Borgo district. Walk along Via della Conciliazione toward St. Peter's Square for your first iconic view of the Basilica. Explore the Castel Sant'Angelo exterior and the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade. This gentle introduction requires no tickets and lets you recover from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Prati Neighborhood: Head to the upscale-casual Prati district (5-minute walk from the hotel) for your first Roman dinner. Explore the lively streets and settle in for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and cornetto at the airport or on arrival — skip a formal breakfast given the midday landing.
meals.lunch: Quick bite near Roma Termini during transit, or a light panino from a Prati deli/alimentari after check-in (€8–12).
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo (Via G. Bettolo, Prati) — a beloved neighborhood trattoria famous for cacio e pepe and Roman classics. Fixed-price dinner ~€25–30 per person including wine. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a Roma Pass at a tabacchi or online to save on transport and museum entry for the week. Confirm Vatican Museums booking for Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel (9:00–13:00): Begin with your pre-booked timed entry to the Vatican Museums. Spend the morning exploring the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Early entry avoids the worst crowds. The museums are a 10-minute walk from your hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Dome Climb (13:30–16:30): Exit the museums and enter St. Peter's Basilica (free entry). Marvel at Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's baldachin. Climb the dome (€8 with stairs, €10 with elevator) for panoramic views over Rome. Rest with a gelato in the piazza afterward.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk (19:00–22:00): Join the guided Trastevere evening food tour. Wander cobblestone streets sampling supplì, artisan cheeses, cured meats, and local wine poured by neighborhood merchants. A perfect immersive introduction to Roman street food culture.

meals.breakfast: Café Pergamino or any nearby Prati bar — espresso and a fresh cornetto (€2–4). A true Roman breakfast standing at the counter.
meals.lunch: Light lunch inside the Vatican Museums café or a quick pizza al taglio slice from a Prati bakery before the afternoon session (€6–10).
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk tour — multiple tastings across several stops cover a full evening meal equivalent.

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums tickets must be booked in advance — walk-up queues can add 2–3 hours. Dress code enforced: covered shoulders and knees required for St. Peter's Basilica. Wear comfortable shoes for the full day of walking.

day_by_day.morning: Pasta-Making Class with a Local Chef (9:30–12:30): Join an intimate hands-on cooking class in a Roman home kitchen. Learn to make cacio e pepe, carbonara, and fresh pasta from scratch using traditional techniques. Classes typically include a sit-down meal of everything you've cooked — a delicious and educational morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Campo de' Fiori & Jewish Ghetto Exploration (14:00–17:30): Walk to the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market square (winding down by afternoon but atmospheric). Continue into Rome's ancient Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins, browse artisan shops, and admire the Great Synagogue exterior. Cross the Tiber to explore Trastevere's daytime character.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Drinks at Gianicolo Hill (18:30–20:00) then Dinner: Walk or take a short taxi up to Gianicolo Hill for the best panoramic sunset view over Rome's rooftops. Descend for a relaxed dinner back in Trastevere.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast included or self-serve before the cooking class. Try Forno Campo de' Fiori for excellent Roman pastries if passing through (€3–6).
meals.lunch: The pasta-making class meal serves as a generous late-morning/early lunch — you eat what you cook (typically included in class fee).
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 (Trastevere) — intimate, family-run trattoria with exceptional cacio e pepe and coda alla vaccinara. Budget ~€30–38 per person with wine. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost €65–90 per person and must be booked in advance. Confirm class location and meeting point when booking. Wednesday afternoon markets are winding down — go for atmosphere rather than shopping.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Tour (9:00–11:00): Take a taxi or bus to Villa Borghese for your pre-booked timed entry (mandatory, strictly 2-hour slots). Marvel at Bernini's breathtaking baroque sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic chiaroscuro paintings. One of Rome's most intimate and spectacular art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Piazza del Popolo (11:30–15:00): After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese park. Rent a rowboat on the lake, or simply relax under the pines. Descend to Piazza del Popolo to visit the twin baroque churches and the Egyptian obelisk. Walk the fashionable Via del Corso for window shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Trevi Fountain & Spanish Steps at Dusk (17:00–20:00): Visit the Trevi Fountain in the golden evening light (less crowded than midday). Toss your coin, then walk uphill to the Spanish Steps for aperitivo hour with a view. Explore the elegant streets of the Tridente neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a quick stop at a neighborhood bar near the hotel before heading to Borghese (€3–6).
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese park — buy supplies from a Prati deli: fresh bread, prosciutto, local cheese, fruit, and a small bottle of wine (€12–16 total). Quintessentially Roman.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio (near the Pantheon) — beloved mid-range Roman restaurant with excellent seafood pasta and grilled meats. ~€35–45 per person. Book ahead.

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets sell out weeks in advance — book online immediately. The gallery is strict about entry times. Consider the Roma Pass for free bus/metro travel to reach Borghese from the Vatican area.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum (9:00–12:30): Head to the ancient heart of Rome with a combined ticket for the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Begin at Palatine Hill for sweeping views over the Forum below. Descend to walk the Via Sacra through the Forum ruins — the Temple of Saturn, Arch of Septimius Severus, and House of the Vestal Virgins. Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum Tour (13:00–15:00) & Celio Neighborhood Stroll: Complete the ancient Rome trifecta with a Colosseum visit (included in combined ticket). Afterward, explore the quiet Celio hill neighborhood nearby — visit the Basilica of San Clemente, which reveals three layers of Roman history underground (€10 entry, extraordinary).
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum at Sunset Experience (18:30–21:00): Return for the magical sunset experience as golden hour light bathes the ruins in warm amber glow. Many visitors miss this — the Forum at dusk is profoundly atmospheric and far less crowded than daytime. Check seasonal opening hours in advance.

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto or any Trastevere café for espresso and pastry before crossing to the ancient center (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Pizzarium Bonci (Prati, or seek the nearest branch) for Rome's finest pizza al taglio by weight — crispy, creative toppings. Budget €10–14. Alternatively, pack a light snack given the afternoon Colosseum visit.
meals.dinner: Osteria Fernanda (Trastevere/Testaccio border) — acclaimed contemporary Roman cuisine with seasonal ingredients. Tasting menu or à la carte ~€40–50 per person. A special Friday evening treat.

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum/Forum/Palatine tickets online well in advance — on-site queues are enormous. The combined ticket is valid for one entry to each site within 24 hours. Sunset re-entry may require a separate reservation — check the official Colosseo website.

day_by_day.morning: Testaccio Market & Neighborhood (9:00–12:00): Take the tram to Rome's most authentic neighborhood food market, Mercato di Testaccio. Browse stalls of seasonal produce, aged cheeses, cured meats, fresh pasta, and street food. Try a supplì, a trapizzino (Roman street food sandwich), and a glass of fresh-squeezed blood orange juice. Explore the working-class neighborhood's street art and Monte Testaccio.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pantheon & Piazza Navona (13:00–17:00): Visit the perfectly preserved ancient Pantheon (timed entry required, €5). Stand beneath the 2,000-year-old oculus and feel the weight of history. Walk to the magnificent Piazza Navona — Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers, baroque churches, and lively street artists. Browse the antique shops along nearby Via dei Coronari.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo Culture & Dinner in the Historic Center (18:30 onwards): Experience Rome's aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar near the Pantheon with Campari Spritz and nibbles. Then enjoy a leisurely final Saturday night dinner in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: Graze through the Testaccio Market itself — this IS breakfast. Sample porchetta, fresh ricotta with honey, and a market-side espresso (€8–12 total for a generous spread).
meals.lunch: Trattoria Da Remo (Testaccio) for Rome's best thin-crust pizza romana — casual, paper tablecloths, exceptional margherita and anchovy pizza. ~€15–20 per person with beer.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati, near hotel) or Armando al Pantheon (book far ahead) — classic Roman trattoria near the Pantheon with timeless cacio e pepe and abbacchio. ~€35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Saturday at Testaccio Market is lively but can be crowded — arrive by 9:00–9:30 for the best experience. Pantheon now requires advance timed-entry tickets (book online). Piazza Navona is best in the early evening when the light is soft and the crowds thin slightly.

day_by_day.morning: Sunday Morning at St. Peter's Square & Papal Blessing (10:00–12:00): If the Pope is in residence, attend the Sunday Angelus blessing in St. Peter's Square at noon — a remarkable and free experience. Arrive by 10:00 to secure a good spot. Alternatively, attend a Sunday mass inside St. Peter's Basilica (free, deeply moving in this setting). Afterward, revisit any Vatican highlights you'd like to see again.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir Shopping & Prati Neighborhood Farewell (13:00–16:00): Spend a relaxed final afternoon shopping for gifts in the Prati neighborhood — artisan food shops, bookstores, and boutiques along Via Cola di Rienzo. Pick up local specialties: canned San Marzano tomatoes, dried pasta, Roman sea salt, biscotti, and limoncello to take home.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner in Borgo/Prati (19:00–21:30): End your Roman adventure with a celebratory dinner close to the hotel — savor every last bite of Roman cuisine before departure.

meals.breakfast: Café San Pietro or any Borgo/Prati bar for a final Roman breakfast — espresso standing at the counter, cornetto alla crema. Soak in the ritual one last time (€3–5).
meals.lunch: Il Sorpasso wine bar (Prati) for a relaxed Sunday lunch — excellent cicchetti (small bites), charcuterie boards, and natural wines. ~€20–28 per person. Perfect for a slow, convivial afternoon.
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio (or your favorite spot revisited from the week) — order everything you loved: bruschetta, cacio e pepe, tiramisu, and a final carafe of house Frascati. ~€35–45 per person. Raise a glass to Roma.

day_by_day.notes: The Papal Angelus is cancelled during certain periods — check the Vatican website in advance. Prati shops may have reduced Sunday hours; food shops and restaurants remain open. Begin packing Sunday evening if departing Monday. Keep receipts for any VAT refund eligibility on purchases over €154.95.

The combined ticket grants access to the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill. Strolling the Forum at dusk offers a magical, cinematic connection to 2,000 years of history.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to your boutique stay in the Vatican City / Borgo district. Settle in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity prepared by the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely orientation stroll through the Borgo district and along the Tiber River embankment. Explore the iconic Castel Sant'Angelo at your own pace — its rooftop terrace offers sweeping panoramic views of Rome, perfect for first impressions. Optional private guided entry can be arranged through the hotel concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant welcome dinner at Il Sorpasso or Osteria dell'Angelo, both a short walk from the Borgo — classic Roman trattorias elevated for discerning palates. Enjoy cacio e pepe, coda alla vaccinara, and a curated selection of Lazio wines in a candlelit setting.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (afternoon arrival)
meals.lunch: Light welcome spread at the hotel upon check-in — charcuterie, fresh bread, local cheeses, and prosecco prepared by the property
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Angelo — a beloved neighborhood gem near the Vatican serving authentic Roman cuisine; reserve the chef's tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Private airport transfer should be pre-booked. Ask the hotel concierge to arrange Castel Sant'Angelo skip-the-line tickets in advance. Keep the first evening relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive early-access Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel tour — enter before the general public with a private expert art historian guide. Spend unhurried time in the Gallery of Maps, the Raphael Rooms, and stand in near-silence beneath Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. This is the crown jewel of the trip's art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue into St. Peter's Basilica with your guide, then ascend the dome for extraordinary views over Rome. Afterward, enjoy a leisurely lunch near Piazza Navona. Spend the mid-afternoon exploring Piazza Navona's Baroque fountains and the nearby Palazzo Altemps, a lesser-visited gem housing ancient Greek and Roman sculpture.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar in the historic center — try the terrace at Hotel Raphael for Campari spritzes with views over the Roman skyline. Dinner at Ristorante Il Convivio Troiani, one of Rome's finest Michelin-starred restaurants, offering creative Italian haute cuisine in a Renaissance palazzo setting.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — freshly baked cornetti, seasonal fruit, eggs to order, cappuccino, and fresh-squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio near Piazza Navona — refined Roman classics in an elegant, intimate space; try the house-made tagliolini with black truffle
meals.dinner: Il Convivio Troiani — Michelin-starred tasting menu with sommelier-led wine pairing; reserve well in advance

day_by_day.notes: Early-access Vatican tour typically begins at 7:00–8:00 AM — confirm timing with your tour operator. Dress code enforced at St. Peter's Basilica (covered shoulders and knees required).

day_by_day.morning: Immersive pasta-making class with a local Roman chef in a private home kitchen near the Prati neighborhood. Learn to craft cacio e pepe, carbonara, and amatriciana from scratch using traditional techniques. Includes a market visit to Campo de' Fiori to select fresh ingredients — a sensory feast of colors, aromas, and flavors.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the class, enjoy the fruits of your labor as lunch. Then head to the Borghese Gallery for a private art tour — explore Bernini's extraordinary baroque sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatic masterworks in this intimate villa setting. Borghese requires timed entry; private guided slots offer the most exclusive experience.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Villa Borghese gardens at golden hour — one of Rome's most beautiful green spaces. Descend into the Parioli or Spagna neighborhoods for a sophisticated dinner at Imàgo, the rooftop restaurant of Hotel Hassler at the top of the Spanish Steps, offering panoramic city views and refined Mediterranean cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with a focus on seasonal pastries, local honey, and artisan cold cuts
meals.lunch: The pasta dishes crafted during your morning cooking class, enjoyed with the chef and fellow participants over local wine
meals.dinner: Imàgo at Hotel Hassler — rooftop fine dining with sweeping Roman skyline views; tasting menu featuring modern interpretations of Italian classics paired with an exceptional wine list

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery strictly limits visitors to 2-hour timed slots — book private guided entry months in advance. The cooking class should be arranged through a premium culinary experience provider for an authentic, non-touristy setting.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided visit to the Capitoline Museums — the world's oldest public museums, housing Marcus Aurelius's original bronze equestrian statue, the Capitoline Wolf, and sweeping views over the Roman Forum from the terrace. Your expert guide will bring Rome's layered history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum at Sunset — begin your exploration of the ancient heart of the Roman Empire in the late afternoon to catch the magical golden hour light bathing the ruins in warm amber tones. A private archaeologist guide will narrate the rise and fall of emperors as you walk through temples, basilicas, and the legendary Palatine palaces.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo in the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's authentic culinary quarter. Dinner at Flavio al Velavevodetto, carved into the ancient Monte Testaccio (a hill made entirely of ancient Roman amphora shards), serving deeply traditional Roman cuisine in a theatrical underground setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a special spread of Roman-style maritozzi (cream-filled buns) and local ricotta with honey
meals.lunch: Salumeria Roscioli — Rome's legendary deli-restaurant near Campo de' Fiori; indulge in an extraordinary selection of Italian charcuterie, aged cheeses, and house-made pasta with an outstanding natural wine cellar
meals.dinner: Flavio al Velavevodetto in Testaccio — Roman classics including rigatoni alla pajata, abbacchio al forno, and tiramisù; ask for a table in the cave-like interior carved into the ancient pottery hill

day_by_day.notes: The Forum and Palatine Hill share a combined ticket; private guided access can be arranged for after-hours sunset visits through specialist tour operators — a truly unforgettable experience with the site nearly to yourselves.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Galleria Doria Pamphilj — one of Rome's most magnificent private art collections, still owned by the original noble family. Highlights include Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X and works by Caravaggio, Titian, and Raphael, displayed in opulent gilded galleries. Optionally, arrange a private family member-guided tour for an extraordinary insider perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive food and wine experience: a private sommelier-led tasting at a historic Frascati or Castelli Romani winery in the hills just outside Rome, accessible by private car. Taste indigenous Lazio varietals — Frascati Superiore, Cesanese — paired with local antipasti and seasonal produce.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Rome for the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — wander through the enchanting cobblestone streets sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artisan gelato, cured meats, and local wines at curated stops. This immersive neighborhood experience is best enjoyed at dusk when the golden lantern light transforms Trastevere into something magical.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — focus on local seasonal fruit, Roman-style yogurt with pistachios, and freshly brewed espresso
meals.lunch: At the winery in the Castelli Romani hills — a curated lunch of local antipasti, aged pecorino romano, charcuterie, and freshly baked bread paired with estate wines
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — an intimate, beloved trattoria serving exceptional cacio e pepe and carciofi alla romana; or conclude your food walk with a final seated dinner at Tonnarello for classic Roman pasta in a lively Trastevere piazza setting

day_by_day.notes: The Doria Pamphilj gallery is closed on Thursdays — confirm opening days when booking. Private winery transfer should be arranged through the hotel concierge with a luxury car service. The Trastevere walk is best booked with a premium culinary guide for curated stops beyond the typical tourist trail.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive early-morning visit to the Pantheon — arrive at opening (9:00 AM) before crowds fill this 2,000-year-old architectural marvel. With a private guide, explore the engineering genius of the unreinforced concrete dome, the oculus open to the sky, and the tombs of Raphael and Italian kings. Afterward, browse the antique bookshops and artisan studios of the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private atelier visit — arrange a bespoke experience at a Roman artisan workshop: a leather goods craftsman, a goldsmith, or a custom tailor in the historic center. This premium cultural experience connects you directly with Rome's living craft traditions. Follow with a leisurely walk through the Jewish Ghetto and across Tiber Island.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell pre-dinner cocktails at the rooftop bar of Palazzo Manfredi near the Colosseum — arguably the most dramatic view in Rome, with the illuminated Colosseum filling the entire horizon. Conclude with a grand farewell dinner at La Pergola, Rome's only three-Michelin-starred restaurant atop the Rome Cavalieri hotel, offering a transcendent tasting menu by Chef Heinz Beck with sweeping nighttime city views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Caffè Sant'Eustachio near the Pantheon — widely considered Rome's finest espresso; pair with a warm cornetto alla crema
meals.lunch: Pierluigi in the Regola neighborhood — an elegant, sun-drenched terrace restaurant beloved by Romans and visiting dignitaries; exceptional seafood crudi and house-made pasta
meals.dinner: La Pergola at Rome Cavalieri — three-Michelin-star tasting menu (10+ courses) with world-class wine pairing; one of Italy's greatest dining experiences; reserve months in advance and confirm dress code (jacket required)

day_by_day.notes: La Pergola reservations are among the most sought-after in Italy — book as early as possible, ideally 2–3 months ahead. The Palazzo Manfredi rooftop bar (Aroma Restaurant) also requires advance reservations for sunset cocktail slots.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — a slow, indulgent Roman breakfast at the hotel followed by a peaceful walk along the Tiber to revisit favorite spots: the Ponte Sant'Angelo with its Bernini angels, the Borgo's medieval lanes, or a final espresso at a neighborhood bar like a true Roman. Optional: a private 90-minute Vatican Gardens walk (requires separate booking) for a serene, rarely seen side of the Vatican.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute luxury shopping along Via Condotti and the streets surrounding the Spanish Steps — Bulgari, Valentino, Fendi, and Italian artisan boutiques. Alternatively, visit the MAXXI (National Museum of 21st Century Arts) for a dose of contemporary Italian art and architecture in Zaha Hadid's stunning building. Return to the hotel for luggage collection and private luxury transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry Rome with you: a tin of Roscioli coffee, a bottle of aged Frascati, and memories of the Eternal City at its most magnificent.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final hotel breakfast — request a special send-off spread with Roman pastries, local honey, seasonal fruit, and a celebratory glass of prosecco
meals.lunch: Enoteca Ferrara in Trastevere — a sophisticated wine bar and restaurant with an extraordinary Italian wine list and refined small plates; perfect for a final relaxed lunch
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight — pack a gourmet picnic from Roscioli Salumeria: house-cured meats, aged cheeses, olives, and artisan crackers for the journey home

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport transfer and check-in. The hotel concierge can arrange luggage storage if your flight departs late. Consider purchasing a curated selection of Roman artisan products — olive oil, wine, truffles, and pasta — as edible souvenirs to extend the experience at home.
